broker/mt5_gateway.py
=====================
Thread-safe serialiser for all MetaTrader5 API calls.

The MT5 Python API communicates with the terminal via a Windows named pipe.
Concurrent calls from multiple threads corrupt responses silently.
This gateway funnels every mt5.* call through a single dedicated thread
using a request/response queue pattern.

USAGE:
    gateway = MT5Gateway()
    gateway.start()                          # Initialise + login

    tick = gateway.call(mt5.symbol_info_tick, "EURUSD")
    result = gateway.call(mt5.order_send, request_dict)

    gateway.stop()                           # Clean shutdown

Single-threaded gateway for serialising all MT5 API calls.

All public methods are thread-safe and can be called from any thread.
Internally, each call is submitted to a queue and processed by the
dedicated gateway thread. The calling thread blocks until the result
is ready (or a timeout occurs).

Gateway thread main loop. Processes MT5 requests serially, one at a time.
This is the ONLY thread that executes mt5.* calls after startup.
Returns mt5.AccountInfo namedtuple for the connected account.

Submits an MT5 API call and blocks until the result is returned.

Args:
    fn:      Any mt5.* function (e.g., mt5.order_send, mt5.account_info).
    *args:   Positional arguments forwarded to fn.
    **kwargs:Keyword arguments forwarded to fn.

Returns:
    The return value of fn(*args, **kwargs).

Raises:
    RuntimeError:  If the gateway thread is not running.
    Exception:     Any exception raised inside fn is re-raised here.

core/config.py
==============
Centralized configuration for Quant Predator v2.1.

CHANGELOG v2.1 — post training-run-1 diagnostic fixes:
  ENTRY_COST:      -0.30 → -0.05   CRITICAL FIX: run-1 was 1.84 trades/day
                                   (already within 2-3/day target). -0.30 would
                                   have crushed frequency to ~0.4/day. -0.05
                                   creates a quality filter without killing volume.
  LEARNING_RATE:   3e-4  → 1e-4   clip_fraction was 0.374 (thrashing). Target <0.15.
  N_STEPS:         4096  → 2048   More frequent, stable PPO updates.
  CLIP_RANGE:      0.20  → 0.15   Constrain per-update policy shift.
  ENT_COEF:        0.05  → 0.08   Encourage broader exploration.
  BATCH_SIZE:      512   → 256    More stable LSTM gradient updates.
  TOTAL_TIMESTEPS: 1.5M  → 2.5M   More training at the stabilized LR.
  MIN_RR_RATIO:    1.0   → 2.0    Raise structural quality gate.
  LR_SCHEDULE:     constant → linear decay 1e-4 → 1e-5.
  MAX_GRAD_NORM:   default → 0.5  Explicit gradient clipping.

NEW in v2.1:
  RewardConfig   — entry cost, patience bonus, MTF gate, session mult.
  WandbConfig    — experiment tracking configuration.
XM broker execution parameters.

PPO + LSTM hyperparameters.

OBSERVATION SPACE:
  Market window : 35 features × 24 bars = 840 dimensions
  State scalars : 2 (current_position, floating_profit_normalized)
  Total OBS_DIM : 842

ARCHITECTURE:
  OBS (842) → LSTM(24×35 → hidden 128) → concat state (2) → (130)
            → MLP [256, 128] → action (3) / value (1)

v2.1 CHANGES vs v2.0:
  LEARNING_RATE  3e-4 → 1e-4   (clip_fraction=0.374 in run 1 — thrashing)
  LR_END         new  = 1e-5   (linear decay gives fine-tuning at end)
  N_STEPS        4096 → 2048   (more frequent stable updates)
  CLIP_RANGE     0.20 → 0.15   (tighter per-update constraint)
  ENT_COEF       0.05 → 0.08   (more exploration)
  BATCH_SIZE     512  → 256    (stable LSTM gradient updates)
  TOTAL_TS       1.5M → 2.5M   (more training at stable LR)
  MAX_GRAD_NORM  new  = 0.5    (explicit gradient clipping)
  MIN_RR_RATIO   1.0  → 2.0    (raise structural quality gate)

Hyperparameter search configuration.

HOW TO USE:
  python engine/optuna_search.py

SEARCH SPACE covers both training stability params and reward shaping:
  - learning_rate, clip_range, ent_coef, n_steps, batch_size
  - entry_cost, patience_bonus, mtf_gate_threshold, min_rr_ratio

TRIAL BUDGET:
  Each trial runs TRIAL_TIMESTEPS (short) on the train set,
  then evaluates on the validation set.
  ~15-18 min per trial on RTX 3050.
  N_TRIALS=15 → ~4 hour overnight search.

After search: best params are saved to tools/optuna_best_eurusd.json
and printed for you to manually update ModelConfig/RewardConfig.

Reward shaping targeting trade quality, not volume suppression.

CRITICAL LESSON FROM RUN 1:
  Run 1 made 1.84 trades/day — already inside the 2-3/day target.
  The original -0.30 ENTRY_COST would have crushed frequency to ~0.4/day.
  ENTRY_COST is set to -0.05: just large enough to discourage
  low-confidence entries, not large enough to silence the model.

ENTRY_COST MATH:
  At 2:1 R:R, minimum win rate to justify entry:
    0 = P×2.0 - (1-P)×1.0 - 0.05  →  P > 35%  (vs 33% baseline)
  Reasonable quality gate without destroying frequency.

PATIENCE_BONUS accumulation:
  8 flat bars between trades: 8 × 0.002 = +0.016
  This offsets the entry cost 3× over a typical inter-trade gap,
  rewarding the model for waiting for genuine setups.

Forex session hours in UTC.

XM broker offset: typically UTC+2 (winter) / UTC+3 (summer EET).
If timestamps are in broker time, subtract the offset from all values.
Verify: compare mt5.symbol_info_tick().time vs datetime.now(timezone.utc).

Weights & Biases experiment tracking configuration.

SETUP (one-time):

Structured logging for Quant Predator v2.

Replaces all bare print() calls throughout the codebase with leveled,

Quant Predator v2 — Data fetching and feature engineering package.

data/feature_engineer.py
========================
Multi-Timeframe Feature Engineering Pipeline for Quant Predator v2.

This module is the single source of truth for ALL feature computation.
It is called identically during training, backtesting, and live inference
to guarantee zero train/serve skew.

DESIGN PRINCIPLES:
    1. STATIONARITY — Every feature is price-scale agnostic.
       No absolute EMA/BB/price levels are included. All continuous features
       are expressed as ratios, percentages, or bounded indices.

    2. ZERO LOOKAHEAD BIAS — All computations use only past data.
       rolling() uses center=False. HTF data is shifted 1 period before
       merging. The unmitigated FVG tracker reads only historical bars.

    3. IDENTICAL BEHAVIOUR — The DataFrame output has the same column
       schema and dtypes regardless of whether the input is 50,000 training
       bars or a 6,025-bar live inference window.

OUTPUT FEATURE SET (35 stationary features):
    ┌─────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ Category        │ Features                                             │
    ├─────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │ H1 Base         │ ATRr_14, RSI_14, macd_norm, macd_signal_norm,        │
    │                 │ macd_hist_norm, bb_pct, BB_Width,                    │
    │                 │ H1_Trend, ema_50_dist, ema_200_dist                  │
    ├─────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │ Lagged Memory   │ RSI_14_lag{1,2,3}, ATRr_14_lag{1,2,3},              │
    │                 │ macd_norm_lag{1,2,3}                                 │
    ├─────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │ Market Structure│ is_swing_high, is_swing_low,                         │
    │                 │ bull_fvg_active, bear_fvg_active                     │
    ├─────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │ Session Context │ session_asian, session_london, session_ny,           │
    │                 │ session_overlap, day_of_week                         │
    ├─────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │ Volume/Momentum │ rel_volume, close_roc_3, close_roc_12               │
    ├─────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │ HTF Projections │ H4_Trend, H4_ema_dist, D1_Trend, D1_ema_dist        │
    └─────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

UTILITY COLUMN (present in DataFrame, excluded from model features):
    BB_Width_rolling_mean — 100-bar rolling mean used for dynamic position
                            sizing. Excluded in rl_env.py's cols_to_drop.

Computes Higher-TimeFrame trend and EMA distance, then merges back to H1.

ONLY STATIONARY FEATURES are returned (no absolute EMA price levels):
    {prefix}_Trend    : ±1.0 based on EMA50 vs EMA200 crossover
    {prefix}_ema_dist : (close - EMA200) / EMA200 × 100  [percentage]

BIAS PREVENTION via shift(1):
    After computing indicators on the HTF DataFrame, all values are shifted
    forward by 1 HTF period. This means an H1 bar can only access the HTF
    bar that closed BEFORE the H1 bar's period started — never the
    concurrently-open HTF bar. This eliminates HTF lookahead bias.

Args:
    base_df:        H1 OHLCV DataFrame with DatetimeIndex.
    timeframe_str:  Pandas resample offset string ('4h' or '1d').
    prefix:         Column name prefix ('H4' or 'D1').

Returns:
    base_df with two new columns: {prefix}_Trend and {prefix}_ema_dist.

Returns binary active flags AND continuous ATR-normalised distance to
the nearest active FVG zone boundary.

bull_fvg_dist_atr:
    When a bullish FVG is active: (close - zone_bottom) / ATR
    Negative = price below the gap (approaching from below — ideal entry)
    Positive = price inside or above the gap
    Zero     = no active bullish FVG

bear_fvg_dist_atr:
    When a bearish FVG is active: (zone_top - close) / ATR
    Positive = price above the gap (approaching from above — ideal short entry)
    Zero     = no active bearish FVG

Computes the full Multi-Timeframe Feature Matrix from raw H1 OHLCV data.

This function is the single entry point for all feature engineering.
It is called identically in:
    - engine/trainer.py       (training data preparation)
    - engine/backtester.py    (backtest simulation)
    - live_trader.py          (live inference — every H1 bar)

INPUT REQUIREMENTS:
    df must have a DatetimeIndex and columns: open, high, low, close, volume.
    Minimum length: ~5,000 bars (D1 EMA200 warmup needs ~4,800 H1 bars).
    Recommended: 50,000 bars for training, 6,025+ bars for live inference.

OUTPUT:
    DataFrame with all 35 FEATURE_COLUMNS plus original OHLCV columns,
    plus utility column BB_Width_rolling_mean (used for position sizing,
    excluded from model observation by rl_env.py).
    NaN rows are dropped (indicator warmup period removed).
    Returns None if computation fails — caller must handle this.

Args:
    df: Raw H1 OHLCV DataFrame from MT5 with DatetimeIndex.

Returns:
    Feature-enriched DataFrame with NaN rows removed, or None on error.

Validates that a live DataFrame slice is safe to feed to the model.

Called in live_trader.py before constructing the observation vector.
Returns False (and logs the reason) if any check fails, preventing
the model from receiving a corrupted or NaN observation.

Args:
    df: The last WINDOW_SIZE bars from the live feature DataFrame.

Returns:
    True if safe to use; False if the observation should be skipped.

data/fetcher.py
===============
MT5 historical OHLCV data retrieval.

Assumes MT5 is already initialised and logged in by the caller.
This module never calls mt5.initialize() or mt5.login() — connection
lifecycle is managed by live_trader.py or trainer.py at startup.

Fetches historical candlestick data from the MT5 terminal.

MT5's copy_rates_from_pos() returns bars starting from `start_pos`
bars back from the most recent bar, ordered oldest-first.
Position 0 = the most recently opened (potentially unclosed) bar.
Position 1 = the last fully closed bar.

For live signal generation use start_pos=0 (includes open bar).
The open bar is excluded from the signal window in live_trader.py
by using df.iloc[-2] as the most recent confirmed closed bar.

Args:
    symbol:    MT5 instrument symbol (e.g., "EURUSD").
    timeframe: Bar timeframe string (e.g., "H1"). See _TF_MAP for options.
    num_bars:  Number of bars to fetch.
    start_pos: Offset from the most recent bar (0 = include current open bar).

Returns:
    DataFrame with DatetimeIndex and columns:
    open, high, low, close, volume, spread, real_volume.
    Returns None on failure.

engine/optuna_search.py
=======================
Bayesian hyperparameter search for Quant Predator v2.

HOW IT WORKS:
  1. Loads data once from MT5 (expensive — only done once before the study).
  2. Runs N_TRIALS PPO training runs, each with different hyperparameters
     sampled by Optuna's TPE (Tree-structured Parzen Estimator) algorithm.
  3. Each trial trains for TRIAL_TIMESTEPS (short) then evaluates on the
     validation set. Bad trials are pruned early via MedianPruner.
  4. After all trials, prints the best hyperparameter set and writes it
     to tools/optuna_best_eurusd.json.
  5. Optionally logs every trial to W&B for visual comparison.

SEARCH SPACE covers both training stability and reward shaping:
  Training:  learning_rate, clip_range, ent_coef, n_steps, batch_size
  Reward:    entry_cost, patience_bonus, mtf_gate_threshold, min_rr_ratio

RUNTIME (RTX 3050, TRIAL_TIMESTEPS=400k, N_TRIALS=15):
  ~15-18 min per trial  ×  15 trials  ≈  3.5-4.5 hours (run overnight)

USAGE:
  python engine/optuna_search.py

AFTER SEARCH:
  Update ModelConfig and RewardConfig in core/config.py with the
  values from tools/optuna_best_eurusd.json, then retrain with full
  2.5M timesteps: python engine/trainer.py

Reports intermediate validation reward to Optuna every EVAL_FREQ steps.
Allows Optuna to prune (stop early) trials that are clearly underperforming.

This can save 40-60% of total search compute time by cutting off
bad hyperparameter configurations halfway through training.

Returns an Optuna objective callable with data pre-baked in.

Closing over DataFrames avoids re-fetching MT5 data on each trial.

Runs the full Optuna hyperparameter search.

Returns the best params dict, or None on failure.

engine/policy.py
================
Custom LSTM-based feature extractor for the PPO policy.

Defined in its own module so it can be imported identically in both
trainer.py (during training) and live_trader.py (during inference).
SB3 requires the extractor class to be importable at model-load time.

ARCHITECTURE:
    Input (842,) → reshape (24, 35) → LSTM(128, 2 layers)
    → final hidden (128,) → LayerNorm → concat state (2,) → (130,)
    → passed to MLP policy head [256, 128] → actions / value

LSTM sequence encoder that reads the 24-bar market window.

Unlike SB3's RecurrentPPO (which maintains hidden state across steps),
this extractor treats each observation as a self-contained sequence.
The 24 bars are the full context; the LSTM summarises them into a
single 128-dim state vector — analogous to reading a sentence with BERT.

Args:
    observation_space: Passed automatically by SB3.
    lstm_hidden:        Hidden units per LSTM layer.
    n_layers:           Number of stacked LSTM layers.
    dropout:            Dropout between LSTM layers (0 if n_layers=1).
    n_features:         Feature count per time step (must match ModelConfig).
    window_size:        Time steps per observation (must match ModelConfig).

engine/rl_env.py
================
Gymnasium-compatible Reinforcement Learning Trading Environment v2.1.

CHANGES FROM v2.0 (post training-run-1 diagnostics):
    1. REWARD OVERHAUL — Pure P&L reward caused 9.2× overtrading.
       New reward components (all configurable in RewardConfig):
         - Entry cost:       -0.30 per new trade opened
         - Patience bonus:   +0.002 per bar held flat
         - MTF quality gate: -0.20 penalty for |MTF_Alignment| < 2
         - Asian session:     reward × 0.5 multiplier during low-liquidity hours

    2. SESSION FILTER — Asian session entries now incur a reward penalty.
       The model learns that London/NY/Overlap setups are more reliable.
       (Hard block removed — penalty is softer and allows the model to learn.)

    3. MIN R:R RAISED — Gate increased from 1.0:1 to ModelConfig.MIN_RR_RATIO (2.0:1).
       This directly filters the low-quality entries driving 521 trades per test.

    4. MINIMUM HOLD PERIOD — Model cannot exit a position within 3 bars of entry.
       Prevents the 1-bar scalp behaviour observed in training run 1.

    5. LINEAR LR SCHEDULE — Learning rate now decays from 1e-4 to 1e-5 over
       training. Implemented in trainer.py via lr_schedule parameter.

H1 Forex trading environment v2.1.

Key architecture changes vs v2.0:
  - Reward function now penalises overtrading and rewards patience.
  - MTF alignment gate embedded in reward (soft constraint).
  - Session-aware reward multiplier for Asian vs London/NY hours.
  - Minimum holding period prevents degenerate 1-bar scalping.
  - Min R:R gate raised to 2.0:1.
Random episode start — see v2.0 docstring for rationale.

One H1 bar step. Execution order:
    1. Update O(1) swing trackers.
    2. Simulate SL/TP/Breakeven on current candle.
    3. Apply reward shaping (entry cost, patience, MTF, session).
    4. Process entry action if flat and not in minimum hold period.
    5. Advance step and check termination.

Quant Predator v2 — State management and trade reconciliation package.

ledger/reconciler.py
====================
Broker-side trade journal reconstruction from MT5 history.

Rebuilds trade_journal.csv entirely from mt5.history_deals_get().
Run this when the journal is out-of-sync due to connectivity dropout,
bot restart, or manual trades placed outside the bot.

IMPROVEMENTS vs sync_ledger.py v1:
    - Multi-symbol support (not hardcoded to EURUSD)
    - 90-day lookback (was 21 days — too short for monthly reviews)
    - Backup before wipe (no silent data destruction)
    - Guard against empty deal history overwriting valid journal
    - Uses StateManager for atomic write
    - Indicator values preserved from journal if already present

RUN:
    python ledger/reconciler.py

Downloads full deal history from MT5 and rebuilds trade_journal.csv.

PROCESS:
    1. Fetch all deals for the bot's magic number in the lookback window.
    2. Group by position ticket (each round-trip = one position).
    3. Reconstruct entry and exit events with true net P&L.
    4. Backup the existing journal before overwriting.
    5. Write the new journal via StateManager (atomic).

Args:
    symbol:        MT5 symbol to reconcile.
    lookback_days: History window. 90 days covers most trading scenarios.

Returns:
    True on success; False on failure.

ledger/state_manager.py
=======================
Atomic, race-condition-proof state persistence for Quant Predator v2.

DESIGN:
    All file writes use the atomic rename pattern:
        1. Write to a .tmp file in the same directory.
        2. Call os.replace(tmp, target) — atomic on NTFS (Windows).
    This prevents the Streamlit dashboard from ever reading a
    partially-written file and raising JSONDecodeError.

    A threading.Lock guards the trade journal CSV to prevent row
    corruption if future async components share the same process.

Manages all shared state files accessed by both live_trader.py
and the Streamlit dashboard (app/dashboard.py).

Files managed:
    state.json        — Live account metrics (balance, equity, signal, heartbeat)
    config.json       — User preferences (auto_trade, symbol, manual_command)
    trade_journal.csv — Immutable trade ledger (append-only)
    chart_data.csv    — Last N bars for the candlestick chart
Thread-safe append of one row to trade_journal.csv.

Writes data to filepath atomically via tmp file + os.replace.

Windows-specific: os.replace() can intermittently raise
PermissionError (WinError 5 — Access is denied) when antivirus
real-time scanning, the search indexer, or another process (e.g.
the dashboard reading this same file) briefly holds a lock on the
tmp file or the destination. This is almost always transient and

tools/strategy_validator.py
============================
Rule-based strategy baseline validator for Quant Predator v2.

PURPOSE:
  Before spending 90+ minutes training an RL model, answer the fundamental
  question: "Does the feature set contain any exploitable edge at all?"

  A rule-based agent applies simple, hand-crafted entry rules using the same
  features our PPO model has access to. If the rule-based agent can produce
  positive expectancy, the feature set has edge and RL training is justified.
  If even the rules fail, the problem is in the features, not the model.

RULE SET (mirrors what the RL model should learn to approximate):
  LONG  when: MTF_Alignment >= +2  AND  bull_fvg_active == 1  AND  RSI_14 < 65
  SHORT when: MTF_Alignment <= -2  AND  bear_fvg_active == 1  AND  RSI_14 > 35
  R:R gate, SL/TP, and breakeven logic are IDENTICAL to rl_env.py.

OUTPUT:
  Prints a tear sheet comparing rule-based vs the RL model's run-1 results.
  Uses VectorBT for fast portfolio simulation if installed; falls back to
  our native loop backtester otherwise.

USAGE:
  python tools/strategy_validator.py

Applies the hand-crafted entry rules to the feature DataFrame.

Returns:
    (long_entries, short_entries) — boolean Series aligned to df.index.

tools/tear_sheet.py
===================
Institutional performance metrics for Quant Predator v2.

CRITICAL FIX vs v1:
    Sharpe ratio annualisation factor corrected from sqrt(252) to sqrt(6240).
    H1 data produces ~6,240 bars per year (24h × 5 days × 52 weeks).
    The original sqrt(252) assumed DAILY returns, overstating Sharpe by ~5x.
    A backtest Sharpe of 1.0 in v1 = a real Sharpe of ~0.20.

RUN STANDALONE:
    python tools/tear_sheet.py
